study type: Retrospective cohort study with time-trend analysis
outcome: Trends in the proportion of livebirths to non-Portuguese mothers
Trends in the proportion of women aged ≥ 35 years
Trends in prevalence of sociodemographic factors
Trends in prevalence of obstetric factors
Trends in prevalence of healthcare factors
cohort: The study included 2,105,497 livebirths from the Portuguese national birth registry between 1995 and 2014, comparing Portuguese and non-Portuguese mothers.
finding: Sociodemographic, obstetric, and healthcare factors showed divergent time trends and rates of change for Portuguese and non-Portuguese mothers between 1995 and 2014.
mod_finding: The increase in caesarean rate between 1995 and 2014 was higher for non-Portuguese mothers (24.0%-36.1%) than for Portuguese mothers (30.6%-31.6%).
